sources.title: Gabriel Camps, Gaia, Encyclopédie berbère 19 (1998)
sources.note: Original scholarly entry, pp. 2954 to 2955. Direct fetch has Anubis challenge; indexed full paragraphs 1, 3, 5 and 6 checked with exact searches. GYY is the published Punic transliteration; no original glyphs reconstructed. Death dated 206 BCE in paragraph 6. Its abbreviated succession skips Oesalces, so use Livy for that sequence.

sources.title: Livy, History of Rome, Books 27 and 29: Massiva and the Massylian succession
sources.note: Primary Roman literary account in English translation; actual text headings and chapters checked despite the web index’s erroneous Books Nine to Twenty-Six title. Book 27.19 is Massiva, Book 29.29 to 30 succession and return. Livy writes later and portrays Scipio favorably; anecdote is explicitly attributed.

sources.title: J.-M. Lassère, Massinissa, Encyclopédie berbère 30 (2010)
sources.note: Original scholarly analysis; indexed PDF and ResearchGate full-text witness checked. Paragraphs 17 to 19 distinguish uncertain western conquest chronology from better documented eastern expansion. No claim all Numidia unified on one precise day.

sources.title: Gabriel Camps and Salem Chaker, Medracen, Encyclopédie berbère 31 (2010)
sources.note: Full article text directly accessible; original scholarly architectural investigation including Camps’s 1969 examination. Paragraphs 36 to 43 on gallery and cedar beams, 62 to 68 on architecture, radiocarbon and uncertain ownership. Same work as OpenEdition entry 551.

sources.title: The Princeton Encyclopedia of Classical Sites, Cirta (Constantine), Algeria
sources.note: Scholarly site catalogue; indexed full archaeological paragraphs checked. The house dates at least to first century BCE, after Gala. El Hofra inscriptions span languages and periods; do not claim all contemporaneous or universal literacy.

sources.title: Louvre collection AO 5243: fragmentary Punic stela
sources.note: Original museum catalogue indexed in full via search AO 5243 Louvre. Direct fetch failed. Date 225 to 50 BCE; suggested Constantine/El Hofra findspot explicitly marked uncertain. Description gives double-moulded inscription panel and rudder; inscription is a French translation, not displayed Punic glyphs.

sources.title: Emanuele Papi and Francesco Martorella, I granai della Numidia (2007)
sources.note: Original archaeological paper, Antiquités africaines 43, pp. 171 to 186. Direct opening and indexed introduction p. 171 checked. Massinissa’s grain shipments belong to early second century BCE; later Roman granary structures are not attributed to Gala.

sources.title: Les recherches en onomastique libyco-berbère: éléments pour un état des lieux, Insaniyat
sources.note: Algerian CRASC scholarly article; direct text and indexed passage on second Dougga inscription checked. RIL 2 dedication dates to Micipsa year ten, approximately 138 BCE; genealogy Massinissa, Gaia, Zilalsen. Used only to date writing witness, not to conflate with the separate mausoleum inscription RIL 1.

sources.title: Anneke Higgs, The historical development of diamond mining legislation in Griqualand West during the period 1871 to 1880 (2018)
sources.note: Original legal history, Fundamina 24(1), pp. 18 to 56. Direct PDF extraction checked. Use pp. 18 to 22 for chronology and claim dimensions. Its 1873 Crown Colony chronology differs from McGregor exhibition’s 1874; public text uses the securely supported 1871 British territory and 1880 annexation.

sources.title: McGregor Museum, Griqua: Ancestors and Frontiers Galleries
sources.note: Institutional exhibition text directly indexed in full. Historical colonial racial labels are not reproduced. Earlier Griqua communities, multilingual settlement, agriculture and Waterboer are distinct from the later British colony.

sources.title: J. W. Matthews, Incwadi Yami; or, Twenty Years’ Personal Experience in South Africa (1887)
sources.note: Primary account by a doctor and colonial legislator; direct text checked. Racial hierarchy and self-promotion require attribution. Public copy paraphrases water supply, hospital and mission school observations, not the author’s medical diagnoses or racial generalizations.

sources.title: A. E. van der Merwe and colleagues, The history and health of a nineteenth-century migrant mine-worker population from Kimberley (2010)
sources.note: Institutional record of original archaeological study, South African Archaeological Bulletin 65(192), pp. 185 to 195; full abstract checked. Remains interpreted as migrant miners, not every burial securely identified by occupation.

sources.title: Abiodun Salawu, Press and Politics: Contributions of Sol Plaatje to South African Journalism
sources.note: Original research on newspapers; indexed institutional PDF passages checked, especially the Tsala ea Becoana section. Office in Kimberley and initial printing in King William’s Town are distinguished. Do not use conflicting dates for the first issue.

sources.title: Center for Research Libraries, Tsala ea Becoana, 25 February 1911
sources.note: Direct archive catalogue checked: exact title, variant English title, issue date, Kimberley imprint and Tswana/English language. This is a catalogue-attested title, not a claim to have visually read the issue scan.

proposedOverrides.summary: Griqua homeland and diamond region, annexed to the Cape in 1880.

batchIdentityNotes.assessment: Distinct eastern Numidian Massylian ruler Gala/Gaia, died circa 206 BCE, before entire imported interval. Do not alias to all Numidia, Syphax or Massinissa. Public overview and period explicitly warn mismatch. Earlier Medracen and later Cirta evidence labeled; Dougga writing outside polygon explicitly contextualized. No arbitrary founding year or successor geometry inferred.

Independent Griqua communities, British territory from 1871, and Cape regional phase after 1880 are distinct. Imported window extends past political end. Point-in-polygon check puts Griquatown inside but Kimberley outside every imported phase; public overview warns this mismatch. No association with Griqualand East or with the entire Griqua people. Bibliographic conflict over 1873/1874 colony proclamation avoided in public text; Higgs primary legal analysis preferred.
